correctness.rationale: A rank-one multiplier distinguishes any missing support arrow: its nth power is a nonzero singleton projection on one side and zero on the other (n≥2). On a common support, substituting inverse multipliers and taking adjoints reduces the two equations to diagonal phases on both the domain and image. Independently, an increasing partial map cannot repeat a vertex on a nonfixed trajectory: an n-arrow segment must exhaust a rank-n map, while phases disappear on fixed points after the nth power. A rank-n diagonal set containing both endpoints cannot be the domain or image of such a segment; if one endpoint is missing, a shift through the sorted set to the missing endpoint (using the increasing or decreasing trajectory order as appropriate) supplies a multiplier that traverses the phase arrow once. This gives precisely the claimed diagonal test, including n=2. Conjugating the primitive endpoint-supported phase by an increasing map whose initial domain element is 1 retains the phase at every target rank and support; powers generate all phases. Idempotent separation follows by testing the conjugates of singleton projections. Counting the resulting blocks yields the stated class counts, and the rank-(n−1) term is smaller than the rank-n term by O_n(m^−2); the endpoint-supported blocks are smaller by O_n(m^−4). The finite evidence in check_margins.out was inspected, not rerun, and is corroborative only.
